name: wild-willows
author: Bailey Dunning
description: Wild Willows — a cozy nature-restoration life sim, backed by Harper

scripts.build: npm run build:server && npm run build:web
scripts.test:integration: npm run build:server && vitest run --project integration
scripts.test:all: npm run check && npm run test && npm run test:e2e:solo
scripts.ios:sync: npm run build:web && cap sync ios

iosComment: iOS App Store build via Capacitor (see docs/ios-runbook.md). One-time: `npm run ios:add` creates ios/ from the template. Every build: `npm run ios:sync` rebuilds web/ and copies it into the Xcode project, then archive/upload from Xcode (`npm run ios:open`). The webview app is the same offline solo build as desktop; src/solo/iosSaves.ts swaps localStorage saves for durable files via @capacitor/filesystem.
masComment: Mac App Store variant (`npm run desktop:mas`). Inherits `mac` config, so everything notarized-DMG-specific is overridden here: MAS uses the App Sandbox instead of the hardened runtime + notarization, its own entitlements pair, and a provisioning profile from developer.apple.com (put it at build/embedded.provisionprofile — gitignored; CI decodes it from a secret). steamworks.js is excluded: Steam can't run inside the MAS sandbox and electron/steam.js already no-ops when the module is missing. ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=false answers App Store Connect's export-compliance question (HTTPS only).
comment: v1 ships SOLO-ONLY on itch.io: solo runs the game logic in-app against local save files (fully offline), so the desktop app needs no server and no network. The same itch page ALSO hosts a browser-playable demo — a separate static web build (`DEMO=true npm run build:web`, published to the html5 channel by .github/workflows/itch-demo.yml) that plays against the hosted Harper with an offline solo fallback and hard-stops after 5 animals; see src/demo.ts and the README. `steamworks.js` is the only runtime dependency electron-builder must package (native, desktop-only, asarUnpacked). `harper` is a DEV-ONLY tool now (local web dev via `harper dev .`, and the co-op E2E harness) — it is intentionally NOT a production dependency so electron-builder doesn't bundle its heavy/native tree into every platform's app (which also de-risks the cross-platform CI builds). Co-op (hosted Harper) is hidden behind COOP_ENABLED in src/features.ts; flip it on and move `harper` back to `dependencies` if you ship co-op.
